messages:
riley: flagging an incident - private onprem rollout hit a KMS decryption lapse; sidecar served cached key for ~7m. need triage asap. :rotating_light:
priya: cluster: onprem-nyc-west, svc: model-ingestor, approx window 2026-03-21T11:40Z-11:47Z. logs incoming in thread.
noah: paste logs? any sign of auth failure or network hiccup?
riley: logs: ```WARN keystore: KMS call timed out after 1.2s; fallback_to_cache=true; key_id=cust-enc-192
INFO keystore: served cached key (ttl_remaining=11h40m) from sidecar memory```
sec-bot: Incident CREATED INC-2026-0424 severity=P2. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/onprem-kms-fallback. Assigned: eng-security.
jamie: possible root causes: (A) KMS endpoint flap (B) transient firewall/egress rule (C) sidecar bug that prefers cache on soft failures. Which KMS (customer vs hosted)?
bao: customer KMS via private peering to customer-gw. We saw a BGP flap at ~11:39Z per net-alerts. That coincides.
priya: net alerts show peering reset ~11:38Z and reestablished 11:44Z. so window fits. good catch.
noah: immediate actions: 1) purge in-memory cache on all sidecars, 2) block any service from reading cache silently (RBAC/sidecar-config), 3) collect audit trail of decrypt requests, 4) schedule key rotation if cache was exposed.
jamie: how to purge? sidecar exposes admin socket on unix path. command: ```kubectl -n model exec -l app=model-ingestor -- curl -sS --unix-socket /var/run/keystore-admin.sock http://localhost/purge```
riley: running purge now. note: two replicas still serve old cache until restarted. I'll drain and restart sequentially.
priya: I'm pushing a temporary networkpolicy that forces egress to only customer-gw and our kms-replica. snippet: ```apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-kms-only
  namespace: model
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-ingestor
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.250.0.0/24
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: infra
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443```
bao: also adding conntrack tuning on the customer-gw team to avoid spurious resets. pinged them.
noah: audit logging: do we have decrypt failures and fallback events shipped to SIEM? if not, enable high-fidelity forward for the next 24h and copy to secure bucket.
jamie: check RBAC: last week we relaxed sidecar admin role to allow prometheus-scrape. that could allow metrics read but not purge. verify policy doesn't allow anonymous purge.
priya: I reverted the prometheus change earlier today in deploy config (PR #5210) but will double-check the role-binding in cluster.
riley: purge executed on 4/4 sidecars, rolling restart in progress. no 500s from model-ingestor so far.
bao: key rotation kickoff with customer scheduled in 30m. we'll coordinate certs and re-issuance.
noah: adding checklist to incident: [purge-cache] @riley, [apply-netpol] @priya, [rotate-keys] @bao, [audit-forward] @noah, [rbac-audit] @jamie. Target: 45m.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-0424 update: containment=true (cache purged, netpol applied), mitigation=ongoing. Severity=P3 pending forensic.
jamie: action item: add a defensive change to the sidecar: if KMS call fails retry 3x with exponential backoff but don't auto-fallback to cache unless explicit admin override; create flag `ALLOW_CACHE_ON_FAIL=false` default. I'll open PR.
priya: also recommend we add liveness check on the KMS peering; if peering down, triage before serving requests requiring decryption.
bao: agreed. I'll coordinate with networking team on BGP monitoring alerts to create a paging rule for KMS peering flaps.
riley: drafting post-incident note with timeline and artifacts; will include SIEM export and kube events. ETA EOD. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
